concepts.name: CLIP
concepts.summary: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining: trains an image encoder and a text encoder jointly into a shared embedding space. From a batch of N image-caption pairs it builds an N x N cosine-similarity matrix; the diagonal holds the correct pairs. Trained WITH text, so its features are language-aligned and semantic -- strong for zero-shot classification, retrieval, and VLM input, and it is Stable Diffusion's text encoder. Weaker at pixel-precise spatial localization because caption supervision is image-level.

concepts.name: Contrastive Loss (Softmax Cross-Entropy)
concepts.summary: CLIP's objective: softmax cross-entropy over each row and each column of the N x N similarity matrix, driving the diagonal high and off-diagonal low. For each image its true caption is the positive; the other N-1 captions in the batch are negatives. A RELATIVE question -- 'which of these N matches best?' -- so the candidates compete and the negatives are the entire source of learning signal. Softmax over a single element is 1.0 always, so training needs many negatives.

concepts.name: Batch Coupling
concepts.summary: The consequence of softmax normalizing over the whole batch: every pair's loss depends on all the others, so the batch is coupled. This forces global normalization (an expensive all-gather across GPUs in distributed training) and makes quality depend heavily on large batch sizes -- more negatives means sharper signal, so CLIP trained at batches of ~32K. Exactly the cost SigLIP removes by switching to a per-pair sigmoid loss.
